quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When using a library catalog to locate nonfiction research materials, how does the Dewey Decimal Classification system organize books on the shelves?
quiz_item.question: When using a library catalog to locate nonfiction research materials, how does the Dewey Decimal Classification system organize books on the shelves?
options: A. Alphabetically by the publisher's city of origin, followed by the book's page count.
B. Chronologically by the year the book was acquired by the local library branch.
C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
D. By cover size and binding color so reference encyclopedias are shelved next to paperback fiction.
choices: A. Alphabetically by the publisher's city of origin, followed by the book's page count.
B. Chronologically by the year the book was acquired by the local library branch.
C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
D. By cover size and binding color so reference encyclopedias are shelved next to paperback fiction.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The Dewey Decimal system groups nonfiction books by subject using three-digit numbers (000-999) and decimal extensions, making it easy to browse related works on the same topic.
